overview:
Summer Lee seeks another term in a Pittsburgh-area district that leans about ten points Democratic. She enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.6 million and holding about $1.7 million on hand, while Republican James Hayes has raised under $65,000 and reports only a few thousand dollars in cash. Prediction markets give Lee roughly a 98 percent chance of winning, and no meaningful outside spending has materialized against her.

With no public general-election polling available, the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap, all of which point the same way. A margin of about twenty-one points carries some uncertainty in an ordinary year, but the alignment of every available signal makes an upset unlikely. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
